resolves: CR1-038 unresolved: 'Whether Türkiye has an IEO national organiser'
subject: International Economics Olympiad — Türkiye route
answer: YES — Türkiye participates and has a named national selection competition.
participated_2026_evidence: The official IEO country page for Türkiye lists a 2026 contestant roster (five contestants), so participation is current, not historical.
partner_status_verbatim: 'No active long-term partners. For information on the country's participation in the upcoming Olympiad, check the yearly website or contact us at Info@ieo-official.org.'
partner_status_note: Worth carrying: IEO itself flags that Türkiye has no active long-term partner organisation, and points students to the yearly site or IEO directly. So the Turkish route exists but is not institutionally anchored the way TÜBİTAK anchors the science olympiads — a student should confirm the current cycle rather than assume continuity.
privacy_decision: The official page publishes the full names of the five 2026 Turkish contestants — who are minors — and a named national coordinator with a personal email address. I have deliberately NOT copied the students' names into any artifact, and have not copied the coordinator's personal email. AGENTS.md §12 (minor-safe design) says to minimise data collection on minors; ORYN has no product need for these names, and the actionable fact for a student is the competition's name and the official country page, both recorded above. The contact is one click away on the source page for anyone who needs it.
fetch_method: Browser pane (WebFetch hit a socket hang up on ieo-official.org)
product_note: This is the shape the corpus needs for every flagship olympiad: not 'IEO exists', but 'in YOUR country the door is called X, and here is the page that proves it'. For a Turkish economics student — ORYN's own worked example throughout AGENTS.md — the actionable step is the Turkey Economics Olympiad, not ieo-official.org.

resolves: CR1-033 unresolved: 'Whether Türkiye has a national IOL organiser'
subject: International Linguistics Olympiad — Türkiye route
answer: YES — Türkiye is listed with a named national olympiad AND is marked Accredited.
accreditation_evidence: The official IOL participating-countries table marks Türkiye with the accredited symbol. The table's own legend reads: 'Accreditation Status: ✅ = Accredited; ❌ = Not Accredited'.
accreditation_note: IMPORTANT DISTINCTION THE TABLE MAKES AND A NAIVE READING WOULD MISS: being listed is NOT the same as being accredited. On the same table the United Arab Emirates is listed with no national olympiad named and is marked NOT accredited. So 'my country appears on the IOL site' does not by itself mean a student has a route. Türkiye has both a named olympiad and accreditation.
selectivity_evidence_note: Retained per CEO request (selectivity_evidence has no column yet): IOL entry is via a national olympiad whose winners form the country team — selection is competitive by construction, not open enrolment. Evidence is the entry mechanism itself plus the accreditation regime.
product_note: Combined with CR1-033: IOL states 'No prior knowledge of linguistics or languages is required'. So for a Turkish student the full actionable chain is now concrete — enter Ulusal Linguistik Olimpiyatı, and no prior linguistics study is needed to try. That is a genuinely low-barrier route into the international olympiad tier for a student with no STEM-olympiad background.
unresolved: The Turkish olympiad's own application window and organiser contact — the IOL table links a contact but I did not open per-country contact details.
IOL age/education eligibility rule still unretrieved (CR1-033).

resolves: CR1-030 unresolved: 'Official confirmation that this ladder feeds the specifically-named international olympiads'; and CR1-039 unresolved: 'Whether Türkiye is an IBO member country and which body runs the national olympiad'
subject: International Biology Olympiad — Türkiye route, and confirmation of the TÜBİTAK → international olympiad link
answer: YES, AND THE LINK IS NOW OFFICIALLY CONFIRMED BY THE INTERNATIONAL BODY.
ibo_listing_verbatim: 'Türkiye: National Biology Olympiad — Established since 1993 — Official website — Turkish'
the_key_finding: On IBO's own member list, the 'Official website' link for Türkiye's National Biology Olympiad points to **https://bilimolimpiyatlari.tubitak.gov.tr/tr** — exactly the TÜBİTAK Bilim Olimpiyatları site recorded as CR1-030. So the IBO, as the international authority, confirms that the TÜBİTAK olympiad ladder IS Türkiye's route to the International Biology Olympiad.
why_this_method_mattered: I could not confirm this from TÜBİTAK's own page — it says only that medallists advance to 'Bölgesel ve Uluslararası Olimpiyatlar' without naming any. Rather than infer the link (which would have been an assumption dressed as a fact), I checked the OTHER end of it. The international body publishes the national body's URL, which is the authority that can actually settle the question. Closed by evidence, not by plausibility.
national_olympiad_name: National Biology Olympiad (TÜBİTAK Bilim Olimpiyatları, Biyoloji branch)
identity_caution: The same page lists 'Turkmenistan: Turkmen National Biology Olympiad' immediately above Türkiye. Second time tonight a substring match on 'turk' would have produced the wrong country — I read the entries rather than matching the string.
selectivity_evidence_note: Retained per CEO request: IBO entry requires winning the national olympiad ('you have to win the Biology Olympiad in your country or region'), max four per country, and participation is capped at twice per student. Selection is competitive by construction — this is the evidence a selectivity exemption would rest on if a column existed to store it.
caveat_still_open: This confirms the route for BIOLOGY specifically. It does NOT by itself prove the same for IMO/IPhO/IChO/IOI, even though TÜBİTAK runs those branches too. Each should be confirmed the same way — from the international body's own country list — rather than generalised from this one.
and_the_ibo_school_rule: Note this sharpens the open IBO question in CR1-039: Türkiye has been an IBO member since 1993 and its route runs through TÜBİTAK, whose olympiad is open to all Türkiye/KKTC high schoolers including Fen Lisesi students. That makes the literal reading of IBO's 'not specific for STEM or biology' school rule even harder to sustain — but it still does not resolve it, and the question stays open for the IBO office.

why_it_matters: TWO INDEPENDENT INTERNATIONAL BODIES (IBO and IMO) now separately name the same TÜBİTAK site as Türkiye's national route. That is much stronger than either alone, and it was obtained without TÜBİTAK ever naming them — I checked the authority that can actually settle the question rather than the one that merely implies it.
generalisation_caution: This now holds for BIOLOGY and MATHEMATICS. TÜBİTAK also runs Physics, Chemistry, Computer Science, Astronomy and Geography branches, and the same link almost certainly exists for IPhO/IChO/IOI — but 'almost certainly' is not evidence. Each remaining body should be confirmed from its own country listing before being published. I am recording two confirmed, not five assumed.
contact_note: The IMO country page also publishes a named academic contact email at a Turkish university. Not copied here — ORYN's actionable fact is the national route and the country page URL, and the contact is one click away on the source for anyone who needs it. Same minimisation stance as CR1-070.

selectivity_evidence_note: Retained per CEO request: IMO §2.1 'Participation in an IMO is by invitation only'; §2.2 contestants 'should be selected through that Country's national Mathematical Olympiad or equivalent selection programme'; max six contestants per country. Selection is competitive by construction.
product_note: Together with CR1-030, CR1-072 and CR1-070 this gives ORYN a genuinely actionable Turkish chain for four flagship olympiads: TÜBİTAK Bilim Olimpiyatları (math, biology, + branches) for IMO/IBO, Turkey Economics Olympiad for IEO, Ulusal Linguistik Olimpiyatı for IOL. resolves: CR1-002 unresolved: 'Which international competitions TÜBİTAK sends winners to. §7.1.2 turns on this and the document never names them.'

subject: TÜBİTAK 2204-A → EUCYS: the link is now stated by TÜBİTAK itself
THE_CLOSING_QUOTE: 'Ülkemiz adına yarışmaya katılan projeler ise, TÜBİTAK tarafından 56 yıldır düzenlenen Lise Öğrencileri Araştırma Projeleri Yarışması sonucunda belirleniyor. Projeler, ön değerlendirme, bölge değerlendirmesi, final değerlendirmesi ve uluslararası yarışmalara katılacakların seçilmesi olmak üzere dört aşamadan geçerek seçiliyor.'
translation: 'The projects that take part on behalf of our country are determined as a result of the High School Students Research Projects Competition, which TÜBİTAK has run for 56 years. Projects are selected through four stages: preliminary evaluation, regional evaluation, final evaluation, and the selection of those who will take part in international competitions.'
why_this_settles_it: 'Lise Öğrencileri Araştırma Projeleri Yarışması' is 2204-A by name. TÜBİTAK, on its own site, states that this competition is how Türkiye's EUCYS entrants are chosen. In CR1-141 I wrote that neither side named the other and refused to publish the join; that refusal was correct at the time and the join is now closed from the TÜBİTAK side. Method note: as with IBO and IMO earlier, the answer was on the OTHER end of the link — TÜBİTAK's call document never mentions EUCYS, but its newsroom does.
A_FOURTH_STAGE_I_DID_NOT_HAVE: The quote names FOUR stages, not the three I recorded in CR1-002/CR1-030: ön değerlendirme (preliminary), bölge (regional), final, **and a separate selection of who goes to international competitions**. That fourth stage is decision-critical because §7.1.2's exam-free university placement (sınavsız yerleştirme) requires being SENT by TÜBİTAK to an international competition — which is this stage, not the national final. Winning nationally does not automatically put you on the plane.
the_full_chain_now_evidenced: TÜBİTAK 2204-A (preliminary → regional → final → international selection) → EUCYS → a top-three placing at EUCYS → §7.1.2 sınavsız yerleştirme (placement into a related Turkish university programme WITHOUT the YKS exam). Every link is now supported by a primary source, though the final step's magnitude still lives in the ÖSYM YKS guide and remains unretrieved.
eucys_2025_result_structure: 36th EUCYS, 15-20 September 2025, Riga, Latvia. Türkiye was represented by 3 projects / 6 students. One won 2nd prize in biology; two won a special prize (Ellison Scholars Prize) in engineering.
onward_prizes_worth_recording: The 2nd prize carried €5,000 PLUS fully-funded places at the **London International Youth Science Forum (LIYSF)** and the **Stockholm International Youth Science Forum**. The Ellison Scholars Prize carried a fully-funded trip to the University of Oxford. So EUCYS is not a terminus — it is a hub that opens further international opportunities, which strengthens the case for surfacing the whole chain rather than any single row.
privacy_decision: TÜBİTAK's page names all three prize-winning students. They are secondary-school students, i.e. minors or near-minors. I have NOT copied their names into any ORYN artifact. AGENTS.md §12 (minor-safe design) directs minimising data collection on minors, and the names carry zero product value — the structural facts (what prizes exist, what they carry, how many projects Türkiye sends) are what an advisor needs. Same stance as CR1-070.
fetch_method: Browser pane (WebFetch hit a socket hang up on tubitak.gov.tr)
remaining_caveat: This establishes 2204-A → EUCYS. It does NOT establish that 2204-A is Türkiye's route to Regeneron ISEF, which is a separate claim I flagged in CR1-002 and have still not verified. TÜBİTAK plainly sends winners to more than one international competition ('uluslararası yarışmalar', plural); EUCYS is now confirmed as one of them, not proven to be the only one.
onward_prizes_caveat: These are the 2025 prize structure, as reported by TÜBİTAK for the 36th edition. Prize composition at EUCYS is set per edition and the onward LIYSF / Stockholm / Oxford places must NOT be assumed to recur every year. Treat as 'this is what it carried in 2025', not 'this is what it carries'.

subject: IChO / IPhO / IOI — Türkiye routes NOT confirmed, and why
status: OPEN. Confirmed so far: IMO (CR1-073), IBO (CR1-072), IEO (CR1-070), IOL (CR1-071). Not confirmed: IChO, IPhO, IOI, IOAA, IESO, IJSO, IOAI.
icho_attempt: ichosc.org/countries is the right page — its text reads 'The persons below are the main, long-term contacts for the SC in each country' under a heading 'National Chemistry Olympiad websites'. The country data is NOT in the page DOM: it is rendered from two published Google Sheets embedded via Google Sites. I extracted both underlying URLs from the page source, which is progress the next attempt should not have to repeat.
ioi_attempt: ioinformatics.org returns a TLS certificate error to WebFetch; the Browser pane reaches it but the landing page carries only the latest edition and exposed no country listing. A regulations PDF was readable and gave the eligibility rules (CR1-032), but not a national-body directory.
ipho_attempt: ipho-new.org's landing page is stale relative to today — it still fronts the July 2026 edition — and carries no country/national-body listing. The commonly-cited ipho-unofficial.org is explicitly unofficial and was not used as evidence.
why_i_am_stopping_here_rather_than_guess: TÜBİTAK runs Bilim Olimpiyatları branches in Fizik, Kimya and Bilgisayar (CR1-030), and IBO and IMO both publish bilimolimpiyatlari.tubitak.gov.tr as Türkiye's national route. It is therefore very likely that the same site is Türkiye's route for IChO, IPhO and IOI too. **That is exactly the generalisation I refused to make earlier and am still refusing.** Two confirmed does not make five confirmed; each needs its own international-body page, and the whole value of this work is that a student can be told a route with a source behind it.
how_to_close_each: IChO — read the embedded Google table on ichosc.org/countries (needs a tool that can enter the iframe, or the underlying sheet URL). IPhO — find the IPhO Statutes and any national-liaison directory. IOI — the IOI site historically lists per-country delegations by edition; the regulations PDF does not carry them.
confidence: n/a — this is a record of what could not be established
note: Recorded so the next lane does not repeat the same three dead ends. Each attempt is described with the specific obstacle, not just 'failed'.
icho_sheet_urls_found: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/13SQOb68AhPisPOeDHo2P89fV9rFRylDoN3HuHwQh_oM/htmlembed  (page title confirms: 'National and International Chemistry Olympiad websites')
icho_why_still_blocked: Both sheet URLs load and their titles confirm they are the right documents, but Google renders the cell data inside a further nested frame that the top-level DOM does not expose — `document.querySelectorAll('tr')` returns a single row containing only the sheet tab name. Three approaches tried: WebFetch on the pubhtml URL, browser on the pubhtml URL, browser on the htmlembed URL. All three reach the document and none reach the cells.
how_to_close_icho: Fetch the sheet as CSV rather than HTML — the published-sheet CSV export endpoint, or the sheet's own export URL — which returns plain text with no nested frame. That is the obvious next move and I did not have a tool that would let me construct and read it cleanly this pass.

resolves: CR1-075 / CR1-034: IChO Türkiye route, previously blocked three ways
subject: International Chemistry Olympiad — Türkiye route confirmed, and TÜBİTAK named for a THIRD time by a third international body
answer: CONFIRMED. The IChO's own published long-term-contacts table lists Türkiye, and the institution of its first-named contact is **TÜBİTAK**.
the_entry_verbatim: 'Türkiye | "Arif DASTAN, TÜBİTAK and Ataturk University" | "Yusuf DİLGİN, Çanakkale Onsekiz Mart University" | "Ayfer Kalkan Burat, Istanbul Technical University"'
how_i_finally_got_it: Three earlier attempts failed because ichosc.org renders its country data from Google Sheets embedded through Google Sites, and the cells live in a nested frame the top-level DOM never exposes — WebFetch on the pubhtml URL, a real browser on the pubhtml URL, and a real browser on the htmlembed URL all reached the document and none reached the data. The fix was to stop asking for HTML: I extracted the published-sheet ID from the page source and requested the **CSV export** (`/pub?...&output=csv`), which returns plain text with no frame at all. 97 countries, four columns.
the_lesson: When a page's data is behind a rendering layer, ask for a different REPRESENTATION rather than trying harder at the same one. I had already written this off as blocked and recorded it as such — the record was honest, but the give-up was premature by one idea.
THE_PATTERN_NOW_AT_THREE: IBO (CR1-072), IMO (CR1-073) and now IChO each independently point at TÜBİTAK as Türkiye's national body — IBO and IMO by publishing bilimolimpiyatlari.tubitak.gov.tr as the national link, IChO by naming TÜBİTAK as its first contact's institution. Plus TÜBİTAK's own newsroom confirming EUCYS (CR1-074). Four separate authorities, four separate documents.
still_not_generalising: This now covers Biology, Mathematics and Chemistry. **IPhO, IOI, IOAA, IESO, IJSO and IOAI remain unconfirmed** and I am still not extending the pattern to them by inference. Three confirmed is three confirmed. The cost of checking one more is one CSV fetch; the cost of a wrong claim is a student planning a year around a route that does not exist.
identity_caution_fourth_occurrence: The row directly BELOW Türkiye in the same table is 'Turkmenistan'. That is the fourth time tonight a naive substring match on 'turk' would have returned the wrong country — after the SJWP organiser list, the IBO member list and the IOL country table. In a table sorted alphabetically the two are always adjacent, so this is a systematic trap rather than bad luck.
privacy_decision: The sheet publishes three named individuals with their affiliations for Türkiye, and the equivalent for 97 countries. These are adults in published official roles, so this is less sensitive than the student names I declined to record earlier — but the product-relevant fact is the INSTITUTION, not the individual. I have recorded the institutions and left the personal contact details in the source, where anyone who needs them can find them.
source_note: The CSV is the IChO's own published sheet, linked from ichosc.org/countries — P1, not a third-party mirror.
caveat: The table is headed 'long-term contacts for the SC in each country' — these are the Steering Committee's contact persons, which is strong evidence of national participation but is not itself a statement that TÜBİTAK runs Türkiye's national chemistry olympiad selection. Given TÜBİTAK Bilim Olimpiyatları has a Kimya branch (CR1-030) the join is near-certain, but the sheet proves the contact, not the selection process.

subject: International Physics Olympiad — Türkiye route named by IPhO, but IPhO's own link to it is dead
answer: CONFIRMED IN SUBSTANCE, STALE IN FORM. IPhO's official contacts page lists national physics-olympiad links per country, and Türkiye's points at a **tubitak.gov.tr** URL. That makes IPhO the FOURTH international body to name TÜBİTAK as Türkiye's national route.
three_problems_with_that_entry: **Malformed as published** — it reads 'hhttp://' with a doubled h, so the link is broken in the page source itself, before any server is involved.

**Dead once corrected** — I followed it: `http://www.tubitak.gov.tr/home.do?ot=1&sid=542&pid=453` 302-redirects once to the https equivalent and then the server returns an **empty reply** (curl exit 52, 0 bytes). It does not serve a page.
**The page is stale** — the footer reads '© Copyrights 2019', and the URL shape (`home.do?ot=1&sid=542&pid=453`) is a legacy Java web-app path TÜBİTAK no longer uses.
THE_USABLE_ANSWER: The route is TÜBİTAK; the live address is **https://bilimolimpiyatlari.tubitak.gov.tr/tr** — the same site IBO and IMO both publish for Türkiye (CR1-072, CR1-073), and it carries a **Fizik** branch (CR1-030). So a student is not stranded: IPhO's own page identifies the right organisation, and the working URL for it is already established from two other international bodies.
why_this_matters_beyond_one_link: This is the same defect I found inside ORYN's own corpus (CJSJ's dead `cjsjournal.org`, CR1-014) — **appearing on an international olympiad's official site**. Authoritative sources rot too. It is a concrete argument for the corpus-wide URL liveness sweep: if IPhO's own national-links page has been broken since at least 2019, our records sourced from such pages inherit that rot silently.
and_a_distinction_worth_keeping: Note this is a THIRD distinct failure mode behind a superficially similar symptom, alongside the ones in the synthesis: (a) server blocks bots but serves browsers (maa.org, cee.org); (b) server blocks everyone including archives (Perimeter); (c) domain does not resolve (cjsjournal); and now (d) domain resolves, redirects, then returns an empty reply — a live host with a dead endpoint. Each needs a different conclusion.
pattern_now_at_four: IBO, IMO, IChO and IPhO have each independently identified TÜBİTAK as Türkiye's national body — via a published URL, a published URL, a named contact institution, and a published URL respectively. Four bodies, four documents, four subjects (Biology, Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics).
still_open: IOI, IOAA, IESO, IJSO, IOAI. TÜBİTAK Bilim Olimpiyatları does run a **Bilgisayar** branch, which makes IOI highly likely — but 'highly likely' is exactly what I have declined to publish four times tonight, and I am not starting now.
fetch_method: Browser pane; link liveness checked with curl
confidence_note: High that IPhO names TÜBİTAK. The dead link is verified, not assumed. What I have NOT verified is IPhO's current national-body list — a 2019-dated page may simply be out of date, and TÜBİTAK could in principle no longer be the physics body. Given IBO/IMO/IChO all point at the same place in 2026, that is unlikely, but the IPhO page alone is weak evidence of a CURRENT arrangement.

subject: International Olympiad in Informatics — Türkiye route confirmed. Fifth international body, and the one that names the exact branch page.
answer: CONFIRMED, and more precisely than any of the others. The IOI's official statistics site lists Türkiye's national 'Website' as **https://www.tubitak.gov.tr/tr/olimpiyatlar/ulusal-bilim-olimpiyatlari/icerik-bilgisayar** — TÜBİTAK's Ulusal Bilim Olimpiyatları page for the **Bilgisayar (Computer Science)** branch specifically, not the general olympiad site.
liveness_checked: Both URLs verified live this pass, and they converge: the IOI-published URL returns HTTP 200 after 2 redirects at 56,728 bytes; `https://bilimolimpiyatlari.tubitak.gov.tr/tr` — the URL IBO and IMO publish — returns HTTP 200 with **the identical byte count**. The IOI's branch-specific link resolves into the same TÜBİTAK olympiad site the other bodies name. I checked liveness deliberately after finding IPhO's equivalent link dead (CR1-077).
turkiye_ioi_record: First participation 1993; 33 years participated; 97 contestants to date; 5 gold, 31 silver, 54 bronze, 0 honourable mentions.
record_note: A 33-year unbroken national programme with 90 medals is strong corroboration that this is a live, institutionalised route rather than a historical listing.

resolves: CR1-040 unresolved: 'Whether Türkiye participates [in IJSO] and via which body'
subject: IJSO — Türkiye is listed, but has not sent a team since 2021
answer: LISTED BUT DORMANT. Türkiye appears in IJSO's official participating-countries table, but the attendance grid shows participation in only **4 of 22 editions** and **none since 2021**.
the_grid_read_precisely: IJSO publishes a country × edition table covering 2004-2025 (1st to 22nd IJSO). Türkiye's row shows √ in **2004, 2016, 2019 and 2021** only; every other year is '-'. The four most recent editions (2022 Colombia, 2023 Thailand, 2024 Romania, 2025 Russian Federation) are all '-'.
WHY_THIS_MATTERS_MORE_THAN_A_MISSING_FAC: A naive check — 'is Türkiye on the list?' — returns YES and would have produced a confident recommendation. The honest answer is that a Turkish 14-15 year old currently has **no demonstrated route** to IJSO: no team has gone in five years. Recommending it would send a student looking for a national selection that may not be running.
the_general_lesson: **Listed is not the same as active.** This is the second time tonight the distinction bit: IOL's country table marks the UAE as listed but **Not Accredited** (CR1-071), and here Türkiye is listed but dormant. A country directory answers 'has this country ever taken part', which is a different question from 'can a student there enter this year'. Any corpus field derived from a participation list inherits that ambiguity.
contrast_with_the_confirmed_routes: Compare IOI, where Türkiye shows 33 years of participation, 97 contestants and 90 medals, with a live TÜBİTAK branch URL published by IOI itself. That is an active institutionalised route. IJSO looks superficially similar in a country list and is nothing like it in substance.
what_i_am_NOT_concluding: I am not saying Türkiye cannot enter IJSO. Dormancy is not exclusion — a national body could resume at any time, and IJSO explicitly welcomes newcomers ('New countries may consider participating without any students' appears on IOAA; IJSO has its own newcomer path). What I can say is that there is **no evidence of a current Turkish route**, and that is the honest thing to tell a student.

subject: IESO — Türkiye's route is NOT TÜBİTAK. A different organisation entirely, and a domain-squat warning along the way.
the_entry: IGEO's (International Geoscience Education Organisation) own country directory lists 'Turkey http://tceder.org/'.
WHY_THIS_BREAKS_THE_PATTERN_ON_PURPOSE: Every route found tonight until now converged on TÜBİTAK — IBO, IMO, IChO, IPhO, IOI, IOAI. It would have been easy to assume Earth Science follows the same path, especially since TÜBİTAK's own olympiad does NOT list a Coğrafya/Yer Bilimleri (Earth Science) branch among its nine subjects (CR1-030: Astronomi, Coğrafya, Matematik, Fizik, Kimya, Biyoloji, Bilgisayar, + 2 ortaokul). IESO sits OUTSIDE the TÜBİTAK ladder. Checking this one confirmed the discipline was worth keeping — six-for-six would have been a reasonable moment to start assuming, and the seventh broke the assumption.
organisation_identity: tceder.org — domain suggests a Turkish geology-education association ("TC" + "eder"/association pattern), but I did not open the site to confirm its full name and mandate. Recorded as the operator-published contact, not independently characterised.
DOMAIN_SQUAT_WARNING: The commonly-cited IESO domain **ieso-info.org is NO LONGER THE OLYMPIAD** — it now resolves to an online-gambling ('pokies') site. Anyone who finds that URL in an old bookmark, a cached search result, or a prior year's ORYN record would land on a casino, not a science competition. The correct current domain is **igeoscied.org** (the parent body, IGEO), with IESO under `/activities/ieso-2/`. This is a sharper version of the CJSJ/IPhO link-rot problem: not a dead link, but a LIVE link now serving something else entirely — actively worse, since a dead link at least fails visibly.
recommendation_for_the_corpus: If any existing or future ORYN record for IESO carries ieso-info.org, it must be corrected immediately and flagged as a squatted domain, not merely a stale one.
eligibility_not_retrieved: Age rule, team size and cost were NOT STATED on the pages I reached (`igeoscied.org/activities/ieso-2/`) — this pass focused on closing the national-route question raised by CR1-030's branch list. A full IESO record would need a separate pass.
fetch_method: Browser pane; liveness checked with curl
confidence_note: High confidence on the organisation name and live URL. Low confidence on what tceder.org actually does — not independently opened.
